editorial.headline: Moving Dangerous Cargo Across Indonesia’s Inland Waters
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers hazardous cargo carried by inland waterway, open to foreign investment nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is a specialist inland-water freight operation: carrying dangerous goods on rivers, canals, lakes, swamps and other inland waters, from the loading point through to final unloading. Its stated cargo scope is substantial and specific. It includes hazardous and toxic waste, fuel oil, petroleum, processed petroleum products, and liquefied or compressed gas categories including LPG, LNG and CNG. The work described here is the movement itself across inland waters, with the transport chain running from loading to final discharge.

It is available to businesses registered at micro, small, medium and large scale. That breadth matters because the activity is not framed as a large-operator category alone; the record expressly lists every scale. Nationally, it is marked **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In straightforward terms, the national position allows full foreign ownership of a business undertaking this activity. The cited national PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali requires an equally direct reading. The Bali entry is marked **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK** and is not blocked by the provincial PMA moratorium. The reason given is that, at large scale, the OSS risk is Medium-High/High. That places the activity outside Bali’s stated island-wide, permanent restriction on PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. A foreign investor seeking to register this inland-water transport activity in Bali therefore does not face a moratorium block in this record.

The national and Bali entries answer different parts of the same question. Nationally, the activity is open and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In Bali, the activity is not stopped by the moratorium because of the stated risk position at large scale. No separate Bali foreign-ownership percentage or local-partnership condition is stated. Taken together, the record supports a clean conclusion: this is a genuinely open foreign-investment activity, including in Bali, for the inland-water carriage of the listed dangerous cargoes.
